Update the existing Architecture.md at `c:\Users\jon\Documents\Dev\ReviewLensAI\Architecture.md` to incorporate the security hardening requirements from Requirements.md v1.2. Do NOT rewrite the file from scratch — read it first, then make targeted additions and edits.

## What changed in Requirements.md v1.2

### New acceptance criteria
- **AC-SCRAPE-11**: `review_text` truncated to 2,000 chars at ingestion
- **AC-SCRAPE-12**: Injection pattern detection via configurable blocklist file; detected patterns replaced with `[REMOVED]`; blocklist includes patterns like `IGNORE PREVIOUS`, `SYSTEM:`, `[SYSTEM`, `<instruction>`, etc.
- **AC-SCRAPE-13**: Each review wrapped in `<review id="..." source="amazon-customer-review">` tags at RAG injection time (not at storage time)
- **NFR-6 updated**: Global FastAPI exception handler required; no stack traces, file paths, or env var names in API responses
- **NFR-9**: Injection blocklist is a plain-text file (one pattern per line), configurable via `INJECTION_BLOCKLIST_PATH`, reloaded at startup
- **NFR-10**: Five new env vars — `INJECTION_BLOCKLIST_PATH` (default `./config/injection_blocklist.txt`), `MAX_CHAT_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (default `1000`), `MAX_CHAT_HISTORY_TURNS` (default `10`), `SYSTEM_REMINDER_INTERVAL_TURNS` (default `5`), `BRIGHTDATA_PER_USER_DAILY_LIMIT` (default `5000`)

### API changes
- **POST /datasets/{id}/chat**: Server-side history validation now required — max 10 turns, only `user`/`assistant` roles, `assistant` entries scanned against blocklist, system prompt always re-attached server-side; new error: `422 INVALID_HISTORY`
- **POST /datasets input**: Explicitly SSRF-defended — ASIN extraction is regex-only, no HTTP requests to user-supplied URLs; URLs not matching Amazon domain pattern rejected with `422 INVALID_ASIN`

### System prompt hardened (Section 10.2)
The system prompt now has 13 explicit rules:
- Rule 6: Confidentiality (no prompt disclosure)
- Rule 7: Identity Lock (no persona hijacking)
- Rule 8: Framing Immunity (hypothetical bypass)
- Rule 9: Encoding Immunity (Base64/obfuscation)
- Rule 10: Authority Immunity (override/impersonation)
- Rule 11: Session Persistence (multi-turn drift)
- Rule 12: Language Consistency (multilingual bypass)
- Rule 13: Review Content is Data (indirect injection)
Plus a `[SYSTEM REMINDER]` block re-injected every 5 turns server-side.

### New Section 14: AI Security Hardening
- 14.1: System prompt defense rules table
- 14.2: Multi-turn context drift mitigation (server-side turn counter, reminder injection every 5 turns, history capped at 10, system prompt always first)
- 14.3: Review content sanitization pipeline (truncate → scan → store → wrap at RAG time)
- 14.4: Output safety filter (scope_refused classification + disclosure pattern scan + injection artifact scan)
- 14.5: API input validation table (ASIN regex-only, history limits, role validation, chat message length cap)
- 14.6: Error response security (global exception handler, no internal details in responses)
- 14.7: Per-user scrape budget (`BRIGHTDATA_PER_USER_DAILY_LIMIT`, lower of user limit vs. global limit applies)
- 14.8: Injection monitoring logging (`injection_pattern_detected` boolean added to every Q&A log entry)

### New findings from Security Audit (Section 15)
7 LLM-layer attacks (A-1 through A-7), 4 indirect injection attacks (B-1 through B-4), 4 operational/infrastructure risks (C-1 through C-4). Architecture should reference these as the threat model.

## Confirmed architectural decisions for the security additions

1. **AI security structure**: In-process FastAPI security layer — a dedicated `security/` module inside the backend, NOT an external gateway service
2. **Per-user budget tracking**: Add `user_id` FK column to the existing `scrape_usage` table (no new table)
3. **Blocklist scope**: Applied at all 4 points: review ingestion, user chat messages, assistant history entries, LLM output
4. **Code structure**: New `backend/app/security/` directory with: `input_guard.py`, `output_guard.py`, `history_validator.py`, `blocklist.py`

## What to ADD/UPDATE in Architecture.md

### 1. Add a new "Security Architecture" section
Include:
- Why an in-process security layer was chosen over an external AI gateway (simpler for MVP, no extra network hop, no new service dependency; external gateway recommended as a future enhancement for multi-model scenarios)
- Brief description of each security module
- The 4-point pipeline diagram showing where security checks fire:
  ```
  User Message → [input_guard] → History Validation → RAG Retrieval
                                                          ↓
  Review Text → [review wrapping] → System Prompt + Context
                                                          ↓
                              GPT-4o → [output_guard] → [scope classifier] → API Response
  ```
- Threat model summary table mapping the 15 findings (A-1…C-4) to their mitigations

### 2. Update the directory tree
Add to `backend/app/`:
```
├── security/
│   ├── input_guard.py       # length cap, blocklist scan, encoding check
│   ├── output_guard.py      # disclosure scan, injection artifact scan
│   ├── history_validator.py # turn cap, role validation, assistant entry scan
│   └── blocklist.py         # file-based blocklist loader (startup + reload)
```
Add to root:
```
├── config/
│   └── injection_blocklist.txt   # default blocklist (shipped with app)
```

### 3. Update the data model section
- In `scrape_usage` table: add `user_id INTEGER FK→users.id NOT NULL` column
- Note: global budget = sum all rows in 24h window; per-user budget = same sum filtered by user_id

### 4. Update the RAG pipeline section
- Clarify that review wrapping (`<review id=... source=...>` tags) happens at RAG injection time, not at storage time
- Note that each retrieved chunk passes through the review wrapper before being placed in `{{review_context}}`

### 5. Update the Q&A engine section
- Document the full request processing sequence:
  1. Validate message length (≤ 1,000 chars)
  2. Scan user message against blocklist
  3. Validate history (≤ 10 turns, valid roles, scan assistant entries)
  4. RAG retrieval → wrap reviews
  5. Build system prompt (13 rules + reminder every 5 turns)
  6. GPT-4o call
  7. Output safety filter (disclosure scan + injection artifact scan)
  8. Secondary classification call (scope_refused)
  9. Log: dataset_id, user_id, message_length, scope_refused, latency, injection_pattern_detected
  10. Return response

### 6. Update environment variables table
Add the 5 new vars from NFR-10:
- `INJECTION_BLOCKLIST_PATH` — default `./config/injection_blocklist.txt`
- `MAX_CHAT_MESSAGE_LENGTH` — default `1000`
- `MAX_CHAT_HISTORY_TURNS` — default `10`
- `SYSTEM_REMINDER_INTERVAL_TURNS` — default `5`
- `BRIGHTDATA_PER_USER_DAILY_LIMIT` — default `5000`

### 7. Add a new ADR
**ADR: In-process security layer over external AI gateway**
- Decision: In-process `security/` module
- Context: Section 14 requires input sanitization, output filtering, and history validation for every LLM call
- Alternatives considered: LiteLLM Proxy (external container), PortKey (managed SaaS), dedicated internal microservice
- Rationale: MVP constraint ("buildable in days"), single-service simplicity, no extra network hop or container
- Consequence: When multi-model or multi-tenant LLM routing is needed post-MVP, migrating to LiteLLM Proxy is the recommended path

### 8. Update the future enhancements / migration notes section
Add: "External AI gateway (LiteLLM Proxy) — recommended migration path when multi-model routing or cross-service LLM policy enforcement is required post-MVP"

209	```
210	users ──< sessions
211	users ──< datasets
212	datasets ──< reviews
213	datasets ──< dataset_themes
214	datasets ──< scrape_usage
215	```
216	
217	Constraints:
218	- `(reviews.dataset_id, reviews.external_review_id)` — UNIQUE (upsert key for re-scraping)
219	- `sessions.expires_at` — enforced at the dependency layer, not DB constraint
220	
221	---
222	
223	## 6. API Layer
224	
225	Base URL: `/api/v1`  
226	All endpoints except `POST /auth/login` require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
227	
228	Error envelope: `{"error_code": "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE", "message": "human readable string"}`
229	
230	### Routing Map
231	
232	| Method | Path | Description | Notable Errors |
233	|---|---|---|---|
234	| POST | `/auth/login` | Authenticate; returns session token | 401 |
235	| POST | `/auth/logout` | Invalidate token | 401 |
236	| GET | `/datasets` | List all datasets | — |
237	| POST | `/datasets` | Create dataset + trigger scrape | 422 (validation), 409 (scrape in progress), 429 (budget exceeded) |
238	| GET | `/datasets/{id}` | Full dataset record (used for polling) | 404 |
239	| POST | `/datasets/{id}/rescrape` | Queue rescrape | 202, 409, 429 |
240	| DELETE | `/datasets/{id}` | Delete dataset + cascade | 409 (if scraping in progress) |
241	| GET | `/scrape/rate-limit` | Daily budget status + `next_scrape_available_at` | — |
242	| GET | `/datasets/{id}/reviews` | Paginated, sortable, filterable reviews | 404 |
243	| GET | `/datasets/{id}/summary` | Pre-computed stats, themes, sentiment counts | 404 |
244	| POST | `/datasets/{id}/chat` | RAG Q&A | 404, 400 (not ready) |
245	
246	---
247	
248	## 7. Scraping Pipeline
249	
250	### 7.1 Flow
251	
252	```
253	POST /datasets
254	  └─► Create datasets row (status=pending)
255	  └─► asyncio.create_task(run_scrape_job(dataset_id))
256	       │
257	       ├─ Concurrency check: if any dataset.status == 'scraping' → 409
258	       ├─ Budget check: sum scrape_usage last 24h → if ≥ BRIGHTDATA_DAILY_REVIEW_LIMIT → 429
259	       ├─ Set dataset.status = 'scraping'
260	       │
261	       ├─ BrightDataAdapter.submit_job(asin) → job_id
262	       │
263	       └─ Poll loop (asyncio.sleep + BrightDataAdapter.poll_job):
264	            ├─ status == pending/running → sleep, retry
265	            ├─ status == error → set dataset.status='error', store error_message
266	            └─ status == complete:
267	                 ├─ BrightDataAdapter.fetch_results(job_id) → list[RawReview]
268	                 ├─ Upsert reviews into DB (on conflict external_review_id+dataset_id: update)
269	                 ├─ Apply sentiment_label from star_rating
270	                 ├─ Record scrape_usage row
271	                 ├─ Trigger ingest pipeline (embed + index + themes)
272	                 └─ Set dataset.status = 'ready'
273	```
274	
275	### 7.2 ScraperProvider Interface
276	
277	```python
278	class ScraperProvider:
279	    def submit_job(self, asin: str) -> str: ...
280	    # Returns job_id string
281	
282	    def poll_job(self, job_id: str) -> JobStatus: ...
283	    # JobStatus enum: pending | running | complete | error
284	
285	    def fetch_results(self, job_id: str) -> list[RawReview]: ...
286	    # RawReview is a dataclass/TypedDict of raw scraped fields
287	```
288	
289	MVP implementation: `BrightDataAdapter` — reads `BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY` and `BRIGHTDATA_DATASET_ID` from env. Max reviews per job capped by `BRIGHTDATA_MAX_REVIEWS_PER_ASIN`.
290	
291	### 7.3 Budget Enforcement
292	
293	The 24-hour rolling budget is checked before job submission:
294	
295	```
296	SELECT SUM(reviews_fetched) FROM scrape_usage
297	WHERE scraped_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
298	```
299	
300	Written as `datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(hours=24)` to stay PostgreSQL-compatible (no SQLite-specific date functions). If sum + estimated new fetch ≥ `BRIGHTDATA_DAILY_REVIEW_LIMIT`, return 429 with `next_scrape_available_at` (earliest window when budget resets).
301	
302	### 7.4 Frontend Polling
303	
304	React Query calls `GET /datasets/{id}` every 10 seconds while `dataset.status === 'scraping'`. On transition to `ready` or `error`, polling stops and the UI reflects the final state.
305	
306	---
307	
308	## 8. RAG Pipeline
309	
310	### 8.1 Ingest Phase (triggered on scrape completion)
311	
312	```
313	For each review in dataset:
314	  1. Concatenate: "{title}. {body}"
315	  2. Call OpenAI text-embedding-3-small → vector (1536 dims)
316	  3. Upsert into ChromaDB collection: collection_name = f"dataset_{dataset_id}"
317	     - Document ID: review.id (UUID string)
318	     - Embedding: vector
319	     - Metadata: { dataset_id, review_id, star_rating, sentiment_label, review_date }
320	
321	Batching: process in chunks of 100 to respect API rate limits.
322	ChromaDB uses cosine similarity by default.
323	```
324	
325	### 8.2 Query Phase (at POST /datasets/{id}/chat)
326	
327	```
328	1. Embed user message via text-embedding-3-small → query vector
329	2. Query ChromaDB collection for dataset_{id}:
330	     results = collection.query(query_embeddings=[query_vector], n_results=K)
331	     K = 20 (configurable via RAG_TOP_K env var, default 20)
332	3. Build review_context: concatenate top-K review bodies with metadata headers
333	4. Inject into system prompt template
334	5. Call GPT-4o with system + user messages
335	6. Run scope-refusal classification (see §9)
336	7. Return { reply, scope_refused }
337	```
338	
339	---
340	
341	## 9. Q&A Engine and Scope Guard
342	
343	### 9.1 System Prompt Template
344	
345	The following template is used verbatim for all chat requests:
346	
347	```
348	You are ReviewLens, an AI assistant that helps analysts understand Amazon product reviews.
349	
350	You have been provided with a set of real customer reviews for a specific product. Your role is to answer questions about these reviews — summarizing opinions, identifying patterns, quoting specific reviewers, and surfacing insights.
351	
352	STRICT RULES:
353	1. You MUST only answer questions based on the review data provided below.
354	2. You MUST NOT answer questions about topics unrelated to the provided reviews.
355	3. You MUST NOT use any external knowledge about the product, brand, or market beyond what appears in the reviews.
356	4. If the user asks a question that cannot be answered from the reviews, respond: "I can only answer questions based on the ingested review data for this product. That information isn't available in the reviews."
357	5. Do not speculate, fabricate, or infer facts not present in the reviews.
358	
359	REVIEW DATA:
360	{{review_context}}
361	
362	Answer the analyst's question based solely on the reviews above.
363	```
364	
365	### 9.2 Scope Refusal Detection
366	
367	After the primary GPT-4o response is received, a secondary lightweight LLM classification call is made:
368	
369	```
370	System: You are a classifier. Answer only YES or NO.
371	User:   Did the following AI response refuse to answer because the question was
372	        out of scope (i.e., not answerable from product reviews)?
373	
374	        Response: "{primary_response}"
375	
376	        Answer YES if it refused. Answer NO if it answered normally.
377	```
378	
379	- If classification returns `YES` → `scope_refused: true` in API response
380	- Classification model: use a cheaper/faster model (e.g., `gpt-4o-mini`)
381	- String matching is explicitly NOT used — secondary call is the sole detection mechanism
382	
383	### 9.3 Audit Logging
384	
385	Every chat request appends a JSON line to a local log file (`data/qa_audit.log`):
386	
387	```json
388	{
389	  "timestamp": "2026-05-27T10:00:00Z",
390	  "dataset_id": "uuid",
391	  "user_id": "uuid",
392	  "message_length": 142,
393	  "scope_refused": false,
394	  "response_latency_ms": 1840
395	}
396	```
397	
398	---

400	## 10. Auth and Session Management
401	
402	- Login: `POST /auth/login` with `{email, password}` → verifies bcrypt hash → creates `sessions` row with UUID token and `expires_at = now + 8h` → returns token
403	- Logout: `POST /auth/logout` → deletes session row
404	- Every protected request: FastAPI dependency resolves `Authorization: Bearer <token>` → queries `sessions` table → checks `expires_at` → injects `current_user` into handler
405	- Sessions are not rotated on use; expiry is absolute from creation (8 hours)
406	- No refresh tokens in MVP
407	- Password hashing: `bcrypt` via `passlib[bcrypt]`
408	
409	---
410	
411	## 11. Theme Extraction Pipeline
412	
413	Triggered at the end of the ingest pipeline (after embeddings are stored):
414	
415	```
416	1. Collect all review bodies for dataset_id
417	2. Run TF-IDF vectorizer (scikit-learn) over corpus
418	   - Remove English stop words
419	   - Use 1- and 2-gram range
420	3. Score terms by TF-IDF weight across corpus
421	4. Extract top 20–30 terms/phrases by score
422	5. (Optional) Noun-phrase filter via spaCy if installed
423	6. Upsert into dataset_themes table:
424	   - Delete existing themes for dataset_id
425	   - Insert new rows with theme text, frequency count, rank
426	```
427	
428	Themes are read directly from `dataset_themes` on `GET /datasets/{id}/summary` — no recomputation at read time.

483	---
484	
485	## 14. Key Architectural Decisions (ADR-style)
486	
487	### ADR-001: SQLite for MVP with PostgreSQL-Compatible Queries
488	
489	**Context**: Fast MVP delivery; no Postgres infrastructure needed locally.  
490	**Decision**: Use SQLite via SQLAlchemy 2 async. All queries written with standard SQL constructs (no SQLite-specific functions, no `PRAGMA` in business logic). `DATABASE_URL` is the sole configuration point.  
491	**Consequences**: Near-zero ops overhead for MVP. Migration to PostgreSQL is a connection-string swap + migration replay. Gives up: concurrent write throughput (SQLite serializes writes). Acceptable for a small internal team.
492	
493	### ADR-002: ChromaDB Embedded Rather Than a Separate Vector Service
494	
495	**Context**: Separate vector DB services (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant) add operational surface area.  
496	**Decision**: ChromaDB in embedded mode, persisted to a local directory alongside SQLite.  
497	**Consequences**: Zero network hops for vector queries. Trades off: horizontal scaling of the vector layer is harder. If the backend needs to scale to multiple instances, ChromaDB embedded becomes a bottleneck — migrate to a standalone ChromaDB server or managed vector DB.
498	
499	### ADR-003: asyncio BackgroundTasks Instead of a Task Queue
500	
501	**Context**: Celery + Redis adds broker infrastructure; the MVP is single-process.  
502	**Decision**: `asyncio.create_task` for background scrape jobs. One scrape job at a time enforced via DB status check.  
503	**Consequences**: Simplifies deployment dramatically. Trades off: no persistence of in-flight jobs across restarts (a crash during scraping leaves the dataset in `scraping` status indefinitely — requires a startup cleanup pass). No horizontal worker scaling.
504	
505	### ADR-004: Scope Guard via Secondary LLM Classification
506	
507	**Context**: String matching on refusal phrases is brittle and easily evaded by paraphrase.  
508	**Decision**: After each GPT-4o response, call a lightweight model with a binary YES/NO prompt to classify whether the response was a scope refusal.  
509	**Consequences**: More reliable detection of out-of-scope deflections. Adds one extra API call per chat request (latency and cost). Accepted: internal tool with low chat volume; correctness outweighs cost.
510	
511	### ADR-005: No Per-User Dataset Filtering
512	
513	**Context**: Small internal team; all analysts work on shared review corpus.  
514	**Decision**: `GET /datasets` returns all datasets. No ownership-based access control.  
515	**Consequences**: Simplifies query layer and UI. If the consultancy needs client-isolation (datasets scoped per client/team), this requires adding an `organization_id` to datasets and a corresponding auth scope — tracked as future work.
516	
517	### ADR-006: Monorepo Layout
518	
519	**Context**: One team building both frontend and backend.  
520	**Decision**: Single repo with `/frontend` and `/backend` directories and a root `docker-compose.yml`.  
521	**Consequences**: Unified dependency management, single PR for cross-layer changes, shared `.env.example`. Trades off: build pipelines must selectively trigger on directory changes if CI is added later.
522	
523	---
524	
525	## 15. Future Migration Notes
526	
527	### SQLite → PostgreSQL
528	
529	1. Update `DATABASE_URL` to a Postgres async URL (`postgresql+asyncpg://...`).
530	2. Run `alembic upgrade head` against the new database.
531	3. Migrate data if needed (pg_dump equivalent not available natively — use a one-time migration script).
532	4. No query changes required if the no-SQLite-syntax rule was followed throughout.
533	
534	### ChromaDB Embedded → Standalone / Managed
535	
536	When the backend needs to run on multiple instances (horizontal scaling):
537	- Point `CHROMA_PERSIST_DIR` at a ChromaDB server URL instead of a local path.
538	- Alternatively, evaluate Qdrant, Weaviate, or Pinecone as managed alternatives.
539	- The `services/rag.py` module is the only touchpoint; wrap the ChromaDB client behind an interface for easier swap.
540	
541	### BM25 Fallback
542	
543	If OpenAI embedding costs become significant or latency is unacceptable:
544	- Add a BM25 retriever (e.g., `rank_bm25` library) operating over the `reviews.body` column in SQLite/Postgres.
545	- Implement hybrid retrieval: combine BM25 scores + cosine similarity (RRF or weighted sum).
546	- The `services/rag.py` retrieval step is the sole change point.
547	
548	### ScraperProvider Swap
549	
550	The `ScraperProvider` ABC (`submit_job`, `poll_job`, `fetch_results`) is the provider interface. Adding a new scraping source (e.g., ScrapeOps, Oxylabs) requires only a new concrete class implementing the interface — no changes to ingest or API routing logic.
551	
552	### Task Queue Migration
553	
554	If scrape job volume grows or multi-instance deployment is needed:
555	- Replace `asyncio.create_task` with Celery + Redis (or RQ).
556	- The `services/scraper.py` and `services/ingest.py` logic moves into Celery tasks unchanged.
557	- The `POST /datasets` endpoint enqueues a task instead of calling `asyncio.create_task`.
558

## 14. Security Architecture

### 14.1 Design Decision: In-Process Security Layer

The security subsystem is implemented as a dedicated `backend/app/security/` Python module invoked directly inside the FastAPI request lifecycle. An external AI gateway was rejected for MVP (see ADR-007). The four modules and their responsibilities:

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `blocklist.py` | Loads `INJECTION_BLOCKLIST_PATH` at startup; exposes `scan(text) -> (clean_text, matched: bool)` |
| `input_guard.py` | Enforces `MAX_CHAT_MESSAGE_LENGTH`; calls `blocklist.scan` on user message; checks for encoding obfuscation |
| `output_guard.py` | Scans LLM output for prompt disclosure patterns and injection artifacts before the response is returned |
| `history_validator.py` | Enforces `MAX_CHAT_HISTORY_TURNS`; validates only `user`/`assistant` roles present; calls `blocklist.scan` on each assistant entry |

### 14.2 Security Pipeline (4-Point)

```
User Message → [input_guard] → History Validation → RAG Retrieval
                                                         ↓
Review Text → [review wrapping at RAG time] → System Prompt + Context
                                                         ↓
                             GPT-4o → [output_guard] → [scope classifier] → API Response
```

Security checks fire at four points:
1. **User message** — `input_guard` (length cap + blocklist scan)
2. **History entries** — `history_validator` (turn cap + role check + assistant-entry scan)
3. **Review chunks** — wrapped in `<review>` tags at RAG injection time; already sanitized at ingestion (truncation + blocklist scan)
4. **LLM output** — `output_guard` (disclosure pattern scan + injection artifact scan)

### 14.3 System Prompt Defense

The system prompt contains 13 rules covering: scope restriction (1–5), confidentiality (6), identity lock (7), framing immunity (8), encoding immunity (9), authority immunity (10), session persistence (11), language consistency (12), and review-content-as-data (13). The system prompt is always the first message; clients cannot replace or omit it. A `[SYSTEM REMINDER]` block is re-injected every `SYSTEM_REMINDER_INTERVAL_TURNS` turns server-side.

### 14.4 Error Response Security

A global FastAPI exception handler is required (NFR-6). No stack traces, file paths, module names, or environment variable names may appear in API responses. All errors return the standard envelope: `{"error_code": "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE", "message": "human readable string"}`.

### 14.5 SSRF Defense

ASIN extraction is regex-only. No HTTP requests are made to user-supplied URLs at any point in the `POST /datasets` flow. URLs not matching the Amazon domain pattern are rejected with `422 INVALID_ASIN`.

### 14.6 Threat Model Summary

The threat model is drawn from the Security Audit (Requirements v1.2 §15). Findings are grouped in three categories:

| Finding | Description | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| A-1 | Direct prompt injection via user message | `input_guard` blocklist scan; system prompt rules 6–10 |
| A-2 | Persona hijacking | System prompt rule 7 (Identity Lock) |
| A-3 | Hypothetical/roleplay framing bypass | System prompt rule 8 (Framing Immunity) |
| A-4 | Encoded instruction bypass (Base64/hex) | `input_guard` encoding check; system prompt rule 9 |
| A-5 | Authority/override impersonation | System prompt rule 10 (Authority Immunity) |
| A-6 | Multi-turn context drift | Server-side reminder injection (rule 11 + §14.3) |
| A-7 | Multilingual bypass | System prompt rule 12 (Language Consistency) |
| B-1 | Indirect injection via review body | Ingestion sanitization (truncation + blocklist scan, AC-SCRAPE-11/12); system prompt rule 13 |
| B-2 | Injection via review title or reviewer name | Same ingestion pipeline covers all review fields |
| B-3 | Embedded instructions surviving RAG retrieval | `<review>` wrapper tags signal data boundary; `output_guard` injection artifact scan |
| B-4 | Poisoned assistant history entries | `history_validator` scans all assistant entries before context build |
| C-1 | Prompt disclosure (system prompt leakage) | System prompt rule 6; `output_guard` disclosure pattern scan |
| C-2 | SSRF via ASIN input | Regex-only ASIN extraction; no outbound HTTP to user-supplied URLs |
| C-3 | Internal detail leakage via error responses | Global exception handler (NFR-6); sanitised error envelope |
| C-4 | Scrape budget exhaustion (per-user abuse) | `BRIGHTDATA_PER_USER_DAILY_LIMIT` enforced at budget check; `user_id` FK on `scrape_usage` |

---
